newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Algerie to resume flights to Paris.
newsitem.headline: Air Algerie to resume flights to Paris.

text.p: Algeria's national airline is to resume within two months flights to Paris halted in 1995 in a dispute over security, Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf said on Sunday.

The Algerian news agency APS quoted Attaf as telling Algiers television he notified French authorities on Sunday that Air Algerie agreed to fly to Paris' Charles de Gaulle airport after experts had inspected the facilities.
He said flights would resume in one and a half months to two months.
"Algerian experts...presented Algerian authorities a report concluding that there was no discriminatory measure against our national flag or our citizens flying on our airline," he said.
French Foreign Ministry officials had said talks were on course for Air Algerie to provide three or four round-trip flights a day to Paris beginning around April 1.
Paris ended all flights by French airlines to Algeria following the December 1994 hijacking of an Air France jet in Algiers.
Air Algerie susequently cancelled its flights to Paris in a row over flight security, although it maintained service to the French cities of Lyon and Marseille.

French authorities insisted on transferring Air Algerie's operations for security reasons to an isolated terminal at Charles de Gaulle airport to the north of Paris from Orly airport to the city's south. Air Algerie refused, complaining that the new facilities discriminated against its passengers.

French officials said France had now agreed to move Air Algerie's flights to a regular terminal at Charles de Gaulle, and Algeria was eager to resume services in time for this year's summer flight schedule, which begins in April.
Talks for the resumption of services have dragged on during a period of frayed ties between Paris and its former North African colony.
Paris' ties with Algiers worsened after a wave of bombings in France in 1995, blamed on Moslem fundamentalist rebels angry over alleged French support for the army-backed Algerian authorities.
